title: Daily Life - Talking About a Past Event
audio: mp3/95. Daily Life - Talking About a Past Event.mp3

segments.en: Hello English learners, welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 您好英语学习者，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: And today we have a very special lesson because we're going to be focusing a little bit more on grammar.
segments.zh: 今天我们有一个非常特别的课程，因为我们将更多地关注语法。

segments.en: We're going to look today at the difference between past simple and past progressive or sometimes called past continuous.
segments.zh: 我们今天将看看过去简单和过去渐进或有时称为过去连续之间的区别。

segments.en: So, we are going to take a look at these two structures which are a little bit confusing at times and we're going to be practicing today.
segments.zh: 所以，我们将看看这两个有时有点令人困惑的结构，我们将在今天练习。

segments.en: But before we get started, why don't we take a look at vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 但在我们开始之前，我们为什么不看看词汇预览。

segments.en: Well, this dialogue is all about telling a story in the past and we're going to hear two words in the dialogue that we need to understand the meaning of.
segments.zh: 好吧，这个对话是关于讲述一个过去的故事，我们将在对话中听到我们需要理解其含义的两个词。

segments.en: I haven't seen you in ages.
Okay, so if I tell you, I haven't seen you in ages.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果我告诉你，我已经很久没有见过你了。

segments.en: Basically you haven't seen me in a really long time.
segments.zh: 基本上你已经很久没有见到我了。

segments.en: So, it's a way of exaggerating a little bit.
segments.zh: 所以，这是一种夸大一点的方式。

segments.en: And this word ages, we can use in many different ways like, I've been studying English for ages.
segments.zh: 这个词年龄，我们可以以多种不同的方式使用，例如，我已经学习英语多年了。

segments.en: Or for example, I can say, I haven't been to the dentist in ages.
segments.zh: 或者，例如，我可以说，我已经很久没有去过牙医了。

segments.en: Oh, well, guess you better go, huh?
segments.zh: 哦，好吧，猜猜你最好去吧？

segments.en: So, ages, a very long time.
Now, another phrase, to run into somebody.
segments.zh: 现在，另一个短语，遇到某人。

segments.en: Okay, so if you ran into Matt the other day.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果你前几天遇到马特。

segments.en: Okay, so you didn't plan to meet, you didn't have a date, you just casually on the street met.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你不打算见面，你没有约会，你只是在街上随便见面。

segments.en: Okay, so I ran into your friend the other day.
segments.zh: 好吧，前几天我遇到了你的朋友。

segments.en: We're going to hear both of these in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 我们将在对话中听到这两个。

segments.en: So why don't we get started with dialogue first time.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不第一次开始对话。

segments.en: Yeah, I haven't seen you in ages.
It's funny running into you like this.
segments.zh: 没想到会在这儿碰上你。

segments.en: You know, just last week I ran into Matt as well.
We went out for a couple of beers and the funniest thing happened.
segments.zh: 我们出去喝了几杯啤酒，后来发生了一件特别好笑的事。

segments.en: Well, we were talking and catching up on what we've been doing.
segments.zh: 我们聊起了各自的近况。

segments.en: Talking about work and family when all of a sudden Matt saw a mouse run under the chair and he completely lost it.
segments.zh: 正聊工作和家里人呢，马特突然看见一只老鼠钻到椅子底下，整个人都慌了。

segments.en: He started freaking out and screaming.
Yeah, and the funniest thing was then he jumped onto his chair and started shrieking like a girl.
segments.zh: 最搞笑的是，他一下跳上椅子，尖声叫了起来。

segments.en: All right, very good, so a funny story and as we saw a lot of stuff in the past, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，非常好，一个有趣的故事，因为我们过去看到了很多东西，对吧？

segments.en: That's right and we're going to look at that in a moment but first we've got lots of exciting language to describe when somebody gets really emotional.
segments.zh: 没错，我们将在一瞬间看到它，但首先我们有很多令人兴奋的语言来描述某人何时变得真正情绪化。

segments.en: Okay, so why don't we start now with language takeaway.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们为什么不现在从语言外卖开始。

segments.en: Now in the dialogue, the guy in the story lost it.
segments.zh: 现在在对话中，故事中的人失去了它。

segments.en: So he saw a mouse and he completely lost it.
segments.zh: 所以他看到了一只老鼠，他完全失去了它。

segments.en: Okay, so when you lose something, you lose it.
segments.zh: 好吧，当你失去一些东西时，你会失去它。

segments.en: You're losing control of yourself and your emotion.
segments.zh: 你正在失去对自己和情绪的控制。

segments.en: Okay, so you lose your temper maybe.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你可能会发脾气。

segments.en: So when I lose it, do I just get angry?
segments.zh: 所以当我失去它时，我会生气吗？

segments.en: But it's usually a negative feeling.
segments.zh: 但这通常是一种消极的感觉。

segments.en: Okay, so it's not a good thing to lose it.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以失去它不是一件好事。

segments.en: No, so for example, when I showed my boss the sales figures, he completely lost it.
segments.zh: 不，例如，当我向老板展示销售数据时，他完全失去了它。

segments.en: So that's what lose it means and now our second word is very similar but has a little bit of a difference.
segments.zh: 所以这就是失去它的意思，现在我们的第二个词非常相似，但有一点不同。

segments.en: Now freak out is very similar to lose it, right?
segments.zh: 现在Freak Out非常类似于失去它，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, but why don't we hear an example now of somebody freaking out?
segments.zh: 是的，但为什么我们现在没有听到有人吓坏的例子呢？

segments.en: I don't even want to just, I just want to forget it.
segments.zh: 我什至不想，我只是想忘记它。

segments.en: I just want to forget it.
I'm like, I haven't, have I even finished one sentence?
segments.zh: 我想，我没有，我什至完成了一句话吗？

segments.en: I'm like, give me a high five, baby.
segments.zh: 我想，给我一个高五，宝贝。

segments.en: All right, so we heard this person freaking out and basically it could be losing control or losing your temper but also in a positive way.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们听到这个人吓坏了，基本上它可能是失去控制或发脾气，但也可能以积极的方式。

segments.en: So maybe you're really excited about something that's going to happen.
segments.zh: 所以也许你真的对即将发生的事情感到兴奋。

segments.en: Maybe you're very nervous or you're very excited.
segments.zh: 也许你很紧张，或者你很兴奋。

segments.en: And now moving on to our third word, stare.
segments.zh: 现在继续我们的第三个词，凝视。

segments.en: Now, when you stare at someone or at something.
segments.zh: 现在，当你盯着某人或某事时。

segments.en: You look at and focus at something for a really long time.
segments.zh: 你在很长一段时间内看着并专注于某事。

segments.en: So you are looking at it.
Maybe when we were small, our parents taught us that it's not nice to stare at other people.
segments.zh: 也许当我们很小的时候，我们的父母告诉我们，盯着别人看是不好的。

segments.en: And our final word, when Matt saw the mouse, he started shrieking.
segments.zh: 我们的最后一句话，当马特看到老鼠时，他开始尖叫。

segments.en: Very similar to that movie Shrek.
segments.zh: 与那部电影史莱克非常相似。

segments.en: Well, why don't we listen to an example?
segments.zh: 好吧，我们为什么不听一个例子呢？

segments.en: Okay, so I think shrieking is to shout in a very high pitched voice.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我认为尖叫是用非常高音的声音喊叫。

segments.en: So we saw four really great words in language takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以我们在语言外卖中看到了四个非常棒的词。

segments.en: And why don't we listen now to the dialogue for a second time, a little bit slower.
segments.zh: 为什么我们现在不听第二次对话，慢一点。

segments.en: And then we'll come back and look at the differences between simple past and past progressive.
segments.zh: 然后我们将回来看看简单的过去和过去的渐进式之间的差异。

segments.en: Yeah, I haven't seen you in ages.
It's funny running into you like this.
segments.zh: 没想到会在这儿碰上你。

segments.en: You know, just last week, I ran into Matt as well.
segments.zh: 你知道，就在上周，我也遇到了马特。

segments.en: We went out for a couple of beers and the funniest thing happened.
segments.zh: 我们出去喝了几杯啤酒，后来发生了一件特别好笑的事。

segments.en: Well, we were talking and catching up on what we've been doing.
segments.zh: 我们聊起了各自的近况。

segments.en: Talking about work and family, when all of a sudden, Matt's all mouse run under his chair and he completely lost it.
segments.zh: 谈到工作和家庭，突然间，马特的全鼠鼠跑到了他的椅子下，他完全失去了它。

segments.en: He started freaking out and screaming.
And the funniest thing was that he jumped on his chair and started shrieking like a girl.
segments.zh: 最有趣的是，他跳上椅子，开始像女孩一样尖叫。

segments.en: Okay, so there was a lot of different uses of past tense here in this dialogue, wasn't there?
segments.zh: 好吧，在这个对话中，过去时有很多不同的用途，不是吗？

segments.en: When he was telling a story that happened, he used the past a lot.
segments.zh: 当他讲述一个发生的故事时，他经常使用过去。

segments.en: Well, let's now, as promised, look at past simple and past progressive in Grammar Breakdown.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在，正如所承诺的，让我们看看过去简单和过去语法细分的渐进式。

segments.en: Okay, Marco, before we start our discussion, why don't we hear one example of past simple and one example of past progressive?
segments.zh: 好吧，Marco，在我们开始讨论之前，为什么我们没有听到过去简单和过去进步的一个例子的一个例子？

segments.en: You know, just last week, I ran into Matt as well.
segments.zh: 你知道，就在上周，我也遇到了马特。

segments.en: Well, we were talking and catching up on what we've been doing.
segments.zh: 我们聊起了各自的近况。

segments.en: Okay, so we heard that just last week, I ran into Matt.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们上周听到了，我遇到了马特。

segments.en: So we discussed what run into means.
segments.zh: 所以我们讨论了什么意思。

segments.en: Yep, to meet someone by surprise.
segments.zh: 是的，遇到一个意外的人。

segments.en: And now this structure is the simple past, right?
segments.zh: 而现在这个结构就是简单的过去，对吧？

segments.en: Now the second example that we heard was, we were talking and catching up.
segments.zh: 现在我们听到的第二个例子是，我们正在交谈和追赶。

segments.en: Okay, so let's look at the difference in meaning here.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们看看这里的含义差异。

segments.en: I ran into Matt, happened in the past, right?
segments.zh: 我遇到了马特，发生在过去，对吧？

segments.en: But one moment in the past.
Started and finished all around the same time.

segments.zh: 所以这是一个简单的时刻。

segments.en: Now, the other example is in the past progressive.
segments.zh: 现在，另一个例子是过去的渐进式。

segments.en: So the action was happening for a longer period of time.
segments.zh: 所以这个动作发生了更长的时间。

segments.en: So let's attach some times to this.
segments.zh: 所以让我们附上一些时间。

segments.en: Maybe you ran into Matt at 8.04.
segments.zh: 也许你在 8.04 遇到了马特。

segments.en: And so the action started at 8.04.
But you were talking and catching up from 8.05 until 9.05.
segments.zh: 但是你从 8.05 到 9.05 都在说话和追赶。

segments.en: So you were talking for an hour.
So it's the past progressive you use when the action is happening for a longer period of time.
segments.zh: 因此，当动作发生更长时间时，您会使用过去的渐进式。

segments.en: So to better understand this, let's have another example.
segments.zh: 为了更好地理解这一点，让我们再举一个例子。

segments.en: Matt saw a mouse run under his chair and he completely lost it.
segments.zh: 马特看到一只老鼠在他的椅子下奔跑，他完全失去了它。

segments.en: So as we heard in the example, he saw a mouse run under his chair.
segments.zh: 因此，正如我们在示例中听到的那样，他看到一只老鼠在他的椅子下奔跑。

segments.en: So a quick action that started and finished quickly.
segments.zh: 因此，快速启动和完成的快速操作。

segments.en: He saw the mouse and it ran under the chair.
segments.zh: 他看到了老鼠，它在椅子下跑了。

segments.en: Now, the second example we heard was, everyone was staring and laughing.
segments.zh: 现在，我们听到的第二个例子是，每个人都在盯着和笑。

segments.en: So maybe this happened over four or five minutes.
segments.zh: 所以也许这发生在四五分钟内。

segments.en: So people were looking at him and laughing and talking about how he was screaming like a girl.
segments.zh: 所以人们看着他，笑着谈论他是如何像个女孩一样尖叫的。

segments.en: So that's the main difference between the simple past and the past progressive.
segments.zh: 所以这就是简单的过去和过去渐进的主要区别。

segments.en: The amount of time that the action happened.
Well, now that we understand a little bit more about the past tense, why don't we hear it again in context by listening to the dialogue for a third time.
segments.zh: 好吧，既然我们对过去时有了更多的了解，为什么我们不通过第三次聆听对话在上下文中再次听到它。

segments.en: I haven't seen you in ages.
It's funny running into you like this.
segments.zh: 没想到会在这儿碰上你。

segments.en: You know, just last week I ran into Matt as well.
We went out for a couple of beers and the funniest thing happened.
segments.zh: 我们出去喝了几杯啤酒，后来发生了一件特别好笑的事。

segments.en: Well, we were talking and catching up on what we've been doing, talking about work and family when all of a sudden Matt saw a mouse run under the chair and he completely lost it.
segments.zh: 好吧，当马特突然看到一只老鼠跑到椅子下而他完全失去了它时，我们正在谈论并赶上我们一直在做的事情，谈论工作和家庭。

segments.en: He started freaking out and screaming.
And the funniest thing was, then he jumped onto his chair and started shrieking like a girl.
segments.zh: 最有趣的是，然后他跳到椅子上，开始像女孩一样尖叫。

segments.en: So now that we understand the words and the grammar behind it, there are some interesting phrases here that you can use casually with your friends.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们了解了它背后的单词和语法，这里有一些有趣的短语，你可以随便和你的朋友一起使用。

segments.en: There's actually a lot of great sort of meeting and greeting and saying hello language.
segments.zh: 实际上有很多很棒的见面会和问候语，打招呼。

segments.en: So for example, when they met up, since they were old friends, he said, Hey, Pat.
segments.zh: 所以例如，当他们见面时，因为他们是老朋友，他说，嘿，帕特。

segments.en: So you can use it to get somebody's attention, right?
segments.zh: 所以你可以用它来引起别人的注意，对吧？

segments.en: But in this case, like, Hey, how's it going?
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，就像，嘿，进展如何？

segments.en: So it's a really friendly and informal way of saying hi.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种非常友好和非正式的打招呼方式。

segments.en: And then he asked, how's it going?
So again, this is a way of saying, how are you?
segments.zh: 再说一次，这是一种说法，你好吗？

segments.en: Marco, what's the correct answer to this greeting?
segments.zh: 马可，这个问候的正确答案是什么？

segments.en: Well, well, for example, he said, things are going great.
segments.zh: 好吧，例如，他说，事情进展顺利。

segments.en: You can say, yeah, things are great.
segments.zh: 你可以说，是的，事情很棒。

segments.en: Now, another one that we didn't see in the dialogue, but it's very popular is when somebody asks, Hey, what's up?
segments.zh: 现在，另一个我们在对话中没有看到的，但它很受欢迎是当有人问，嘿，怎么了？

segments.en: So again, what is the right way to answer this question?
segments.zh: 再说一次，回答这个问题的正确方法是什么？

segments.en: So when somebody says, what's up?
You can say, well, not much.
Or if maybe you have news or something that you want to share, you would say, well, I just got back from the doctor's office.
segments.zh: 或者，如果您有新闻或想要分享的内容，您会说，嗯，我刚从医生办公室回来。

segments.en: But you wouldn't say, fine, thank you.
Or you wouldn't say, very good.
Or any of these other common answers to what's up.
segments.zh: 或任何这些其他常见答案中的任何一个。

segments.en: It can be a little bit tricky.
So the rule is, the normal thing to say when someone says, hey, what's up?
segments.zh: 所以规则是，当有人说，嘿，怎么了？

segments.en: So interesting ways of greeting casually with people, right?
segments.zh: 如此有趣的方式与人打招呼的方式，对吧？

segments.en: You wouldn't use this fully with your boss, maybe, or in an office setting.
segments.zh: 您可能不会将其与您的老板或在办公室环境中完全使用。

segments.en: So if you have any other questions or have any other informal greetings that you would like to share with us, come to EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您有任何其他问题或有任何其他非正式问候，您想与我们分享，请访问 englishpod.com。

segments.en: Marco and I are always around to answer your questions and we look forward to hearing from you.
segments.zh: Marco 和我总是在回答您的问题，我们期待收到您的来信。
